newsitem.title: USA: Nebraska corn condition improves slightly on week.
newsitem.headline: Nebraska corn condition improves slightly on week.

text.p: The Nebraska corn crop condition improved slightly during the week ended Sunday and soybean seedings were nearly complete, according to the Nebraska Agricultural Statistics Service.
Corn conditions stood at two percent poor, 18 percent fair, 67 percent good and 13 percent excellent.

Soybean seedings were 97 percent complete, ahead of the year ago pace of 77 percent and above the five year average pace of 80 percent. Soybeans were one percent poor, 24 percent fair, 66 percent good and nine percent excellent.
Winter wheat conditions improved to five percent excellent, 46 percent good, 37 percent fair, 10 percent poor and two percent very poor.
Eighty-six percent of the crop was headed, ahead of 68 percent a year ago and ahead of the 81 percent average pace.
Sorghum seeding was 94 percent complete, ahead of 68 percent a year ago and ahead of the 73 percent average pace.

Alfalfa conditions were six percent very poor, 12 percent poor, 32 percent fair, 48 percent good and two percent excellent. Topsoil moisture levels were two percent very short, 16 percent short, 78 percent adequate and four percent surplus.
